changes: Typed request and response identities retain exact job, lease, worker, registry and resource binding.
Typed workers verify wallet policies and child proofs on CPU before proving each recursive node.
Cached workers retain RAM, managed VRAM and spill reservations across jobs and idle preprocessing; idle workspaces reserve zero CPU slots.
GPU queues drain before job reconciliation; teardown precedes workspace reservation release.
Shared resource limits accept independently admitted hardware capacities; legacy CPU packet bounds remain enforced.
Fleet dispatch explicitly selects the typed DAG path and rejects backend mismatch or missing teardown receipts.
Context calibration reuse requires the same execution backend as the requested trial.
Portable report records expose execution identity and cache counters.

concurrent_fleet.scope: One fresh independently CPU-audited mixed root per GPU, using existing public wallet proofs. Registry preparation and durable host application are excluded.

failed_proving_attempts.reason: Original shared DAG capacity ceiling rejected the admitted 45 GiB worker and 1 GiB coordinator before proving.

result.failure: ValueError: typed worker failed; no automatic retry
result.timing_boundary: worker fixture copy, recursive proving, and independent CPU root audit; registry preparation excluded

known_limits: Each GPU process owns its own DAG and cached worker. Persistent cross-process typed job dispatch and native arrival integration remain open.
The clean GPU journals have not yet been reopened and audited in a fresh CPU process; active proving-worker termination recovery remains unqualified.
These are fresh recursive proofs over retained public wallets, not newly delivered user transactions.
Per-device standalone runs and the concurrent fleet use different CPU and memory assignments. They do not establish a matched speedup.
The new binary uses conservative bootstrap driver/context allowances; smaller calibrated allowances have not been qualified for it.
The two-worker eight-input trial is one repetition. Larger counts, full cold-64 and post-seal timing gates, full-size CPU proving and Mac repetitions remain open.

profile.model_note: Live retained matrices, salts, and readback buffers plus 512 MiB for overlapping temporary mappings. The eight auxiliary mappings include headers; worker cgroups and allocator reservations enforce the full assigned limits.
profile.name: typed-paired-compact-depth-six-bootstrap-v1
profile.readback_note: Candidate direct row-major decoding removes only the second complete readback matrix in preprocessing/main/permutation commitment. Other phase allowances remain conservative. Admission is not full-job qualification; each exact binary and geometry must pass CPU-audited per-GPU qualification under its assigned limits.

scope: Typed inline DAG proving, reusable preprocessing, persistent resource reservations, and concurrent independent roots on two GPUs. Existing public wallet proofs and registry keys are reused.
